common_name: Belle Cook Daylily (Pink Self, Parent of South Pacific)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; this tetraploid Brooker introduction, registered in 2001, carries semi-evergreen foliage and blooms midseason.

directions: Plant in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Belle Cook bears large, six-inch pink self flowers above a green throat, carried on well-branched, two-foot scapes. Registered by Malcolm Brooker in 2001 from a cross of Ed Brown and Seminole Wind, this tetraploid earned the AHS Honorable Mention in 2005 and an Award of Merit in 2008, and was later used, crossed with Seabiscuit, as a parent of South Pacific. Divide congested clumps in spring every few years to maintain vigor and bloom count.

common_name: Seabiscuit Daylily (Light Pink with Citrine Edge, Parent of South Pacific)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; this tetraploid cultivar, registered in 2003 from a seedling crossed with Siloam Ralph Henry, carries fragrant, semi-evergreen, reblooming foliage.

directions: Plant in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Seabiscuit bears large, six-and-a-half-inch, light pink flowers edged in citrine, carried on well-branched, two-and-a-half-foot scapes. Registered in 2003 from a seedling crossed with tetraploid Siloam Ralph Henry, this fragrant tetraploid reblooms on semi-evergreen foliage and was later used, crossed with Belle Cook, as a parent of South Pacific. Divide congested clumps in spring every few years to maintain vigor and bloom count.

common_name: Dragon's Eye Daylily (Pastel Pink with Rose-Red Eyezone, Parent of Gillian)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; this diploid Salter introduction, registered in 1991, carries semi-evergreen, reblooming foliage and blooms midseason to late.

directions: Plant in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Dragon's Eye bears four-inch pastel-pink flowers with a prominent bright rose-red eyezone above a green throat, carried on well-branched, two-foot scapes. Registered by E.H. Salter in 1991 from a cross of Enchanter's Spell and Janice Brown, this reblooming diploid earned the Annie T. Giles Award in 1997, and was later used, crossed with Moonlit Masquerade, as a parent of Gillian. Divide congested clumps in spring every few years to maintain vigor and bloom count.

common_name: Prometheus Revisited Daylily (Raspberry Blend with Rose Watermark, Parent of Electric Ladyland)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; this tetraploid Hanson introduction, registered in 2008, carries semi-evergreen foliage and blooms in the early midseason.

directions: Plant in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Prometheus Revisited bears five-and-a-half-inch, vibrant raspberry-blend flowers with a rose watermark above a chartreuse throat, carried on well-branched, 28-inch scapes. Registered by Curt Hanson in 2008 from a cross of Kissed Off and Enchanting Esmerelda, this tetraploid blooms in the early midseason on semi-evergreen foliage and was later used, crossed with Celestial Virgins, as a parent of Electric Ladyland. Divide congested clumps in spring every few years to maintain vigor and bloom count.
